name: Glycolic acid

lead: Glycolic acid is the smallest alpha hydroxy acid and one of the most widely used chemical exfoliants. Lower-strength products are used at home for dullness and rough texture, and higher concentrations are applied in professional peels.
Studies show improvements in photoaged skin texture and fine lines with regular use, although stronger peels carry greater risk.

paras: By weakening the bonds between surface skin cells, glycolic acid promotes exfoliation, and with repeated use it stimulates epidermal renewal and has been reported to increase dermal collagen and glycosaminoglycans.

Stinging, redness and peeling are frequent, and the skin becomes more sensitive to ultraviolet light, so sunscreen is important. Excess strength or poor technique can cause burns and post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation, especially in darker skin tones.
